title: Import screen doesn't warn that the PIN won't come back after a restore
description:
Surfaced during UAT of LODGY-103. That ticket fixed the actual data gap (hostel/notification/theme prefs now travel with a backup) and made a deliberate, documented decision that the PIN (auth_prefs) does NOT travel - a new phone gets a fresh PIN setup, which is the safer default. That's the right call, but nothing on the Backup & Restore screen tells the warden this before they hit it.

Today's copy (`backup_import_description`): "Pick a previously exported backup file to restore your data - from Google Drive, Downloads, or wherever you saved it. Useful when moving to a new phone." A warden who restores everything and then lands on 'Set up your PIN' with no warning may reasonably wonder if the restore actually worked, right after LODGY-103 specifically improved how complete a restore feels. A one-line note fixes this cheaply.
acceptanceCriteria: Import screen's description (or a note shown right after a successful restore) tells the warden they'll set up a new PIN, before or immediately after they hit that screen - not left to discover it silently
Copy makes clear this is expected/normal, not a sign the restore partially failed

history.note: Found while accepting LODGY-103 - checked backup_import_description in strings.xml and confirmed it says nothing about the PIN reset, even though that's now a documented, deliberate behavior. Low priority - a copy-only fix, not a data or logic gap.
Copy-only fix - no code/logic change needed, just strings.xml + values-hi/strings.xml.

backup_import_description now ends with: "You'll set up a new PIN on this device afterwards - your hostels, tenants and settings all come back, only the PIN doesn't." backup_restart_body now ends with: "You'll be asked to set up a new PIN - that's expected, not a sign anything went wrong." Both satisfy AC #1 (warned before/immediately after hitting the screen) and AC #2 (explicitly framed as expected, not a failure). Hindi strings in values-hi/strings.xml given matching additions for parity. Verified via full test suite (650 tests, 0 failures, coverage gate met) that strings.xml parses and nothing else broke; did not additionally re-verify the two screens rendering on-device this pass (no logic path changed, pure string content).

PASS. Read both strings directly in values/strings.xml (lines 517, 525): backup_import_description and backup_restart_body both now name the PIN reset explicitly and frame it as expected, not a failure - satisfies AC #1 and AC #2 literally. Read values-hi/strings.xml (lines 507, 515) and confirmed the Hindi additions are genuine translations matching the English intent, not left blank or copy-pasted English - maintains this codebase's bilingual parity requirement. No logic changed, no code paths to re-test; full suite green (650 tests, 0 failures, coverage gate met).

Accepted. This is exactly the moment I flagged when I filed the ticket - I'd have hit 'Set up your PIN' right after a restore and wondered if I'd lost something. The new copy tells me upfront (on the Import screen, before I even pick a file) that only the PIN resets and everything else - hostels, tenants, settings - comes back, and the restart dialog repeats the same reassurance right when I'd see the PIN setup screen. Reads calm, not alarming, in both English and Hindi. No further gap.
